sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Hello, Trevor.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 你好，特雷弗。

sentences.en: TREVOR: Hello, Stephanie.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 你好，斯蒂芬妮。

sentences.en: You said you wanted to talk about the course I'm taking on literature for children.3
sentences.zh: 你说过想跟我聊聊我正在修的儿童文学课程。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: That's right.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 没错。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of doing it next year, but I'd like to find out more about it first.
sentences.zh: 我打算明年也选这门课，但想先多了解一些情况。

sentences.en: TREVOR: OK, well, as you probably know, it's a one-year course.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 好的，如你所知，这是一门为期一年的课程。

sentences.en: It's divided into six modules, and you have to take all of them.
sentences.zh: 课程分为六个模块，所有模块都必须修读。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting ones, for me, at least, was about the purpose of children's literature.
sentences.zh: 其中最有趣的一个模块——至少对我而言——是关于儿童文学的功能。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: You mean, whether it should just entertain children or should be educational, as well.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 你的意思是，儿童文学究竟应该仅仅起到娱乐作用，还是也应具备教育功能？

sentences.en: TREVOR: Right, and whether the teaching should be factual - giving them information about the world - or ethical, teaching them values.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 没错，而且还要探讨这种教育功能应侧重于传授事实性知识——即向孩子介绍世界相关信息——还是侧重于伦理道德教育——即向孩子传递价值观。

sentences.en: What's fascinating is that the writer isn't necessarily conscious of the message they're conveying.
sentences.zh: 令人着迷的是，作者未必能意识到自己作品中所传达的信息。

sentences.en: For instance, a story might show a child who has a problem as a result of not doing what an adult has told them to do, implying that children should always obey adults.
sentences.zh: 例如，某个故事可能描写一个孩子因不听从成人指示而遭遇问题，从而暗示儿童应始终服从成人。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: I see what you mean.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 我明白你的意思了。

sentences.en: TREVOR: That module made me realise how important stories are - they can have a significant effect on children as they grow up.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 这个模块让我意识到故事的重要性——它们对孩子成长过程会产生深远影响。

sentences.en: Actually, it inspired me to have a go at it myself, just for my own interest. know I can't compete with the really popular stories, like the Harry Potter books - they're very good, and even young kids like my seven-year-old niece love reading them.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它还激发了我自己尝试创作故事的兴趣，纯粹出于个人爱好。我知道自己无法与《哈利·波特》这类真正畅销的作品相提并论——它们写得非常出色，连我七岁的侄女这样的小孩子都喜欢阅读。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Mm.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 嗯。

sentences.en: I'm very interested in illustrations in stories.
sentences.zh: 我对故事中的插图特别感兴趣。

sentences.en: Is that covered in the in course?
sentences.zh: 课程里会涵盖这部分内容吗？

sentences.en: TREVOR: Yes, there's a module on pictures, and how they're sometimes central to the story.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 是的，有一个专门讲图画的模块，探讨图画有时如何成为故事的核心要素。

sentences.en: Audioscripts
sentences.zh: 听力原文

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: That's good.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 那太好了。

sentences.en: I remember some frightening ones I saw as a child and I can still see them vividly in my mind, years later!
sentences.zh: 我记得小时候看过一些令我害怕的插图，多年后至今仍能清晰地浮现在脑海中！

sentences.en: Pictures can be so powerful, just as powerful as words.
sentences.zh: 图画的力量如此强大，丝毫不亚于文字。

sentences.en: I've always enjoyed drawing, so that's the field I want to go into when I finish the course.
sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢绘画，因此毕业后我想进入这一领域。

sentences.en: I bet that module will be really helpful.
sentences.zh: 我相信那个模块一定会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: TREVOR: I'm sure it will.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 我确信会的。

sentences.en: We also studied comics in that module, but I'm not convinced of their value, not compared with books.
sentences.zh: 我们在该模块中也学习了漫画，但我并不认为漫画有多大价值——至少与图书相比是这样。

sentences.en: One of the great things about words is that you use your imagination, but with a comic you don't have to.
sentences.zh: 文字的一大优势在于能激发你的想象力，而看漫画则无需如此。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: But children are SO used to visual input - on TV, video games, and so on.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 但孩子们早已习惯视觉信息输入——比如电视、电子游戏等等。

sentences.en: There are plenty of kids who wouldn't even try to read a book, so I think comics can serve a really useful purpose.
sentences.zh: 有很多孩子甚至根本不愿尝试读书，所以我认为漫画确实能发挥非常实用的作用。

sentences.en: TREVOR.
sentences.zh: TREVOR.

sentences.en: You mean, it's better to read a comic than a not to read at all?
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，读漫画总比完全不读书要好？

sentences.en: Yes, I suppose you're right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想你说得对。

sentences.en: I just think it's sad when children don't read books.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，当孩子们不读书时，实在令人遗憾。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: What about books for girls and books for boys?
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 那么专为女孩写的书和专为男孩写的书呢？

sentences.en: Does the course go into that?
sentences.zh: 课程里会涉及这方面内容吗？

sentences.en: TREVOR: Yes, there's a module on it.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 是的，有一个专门的模块讨论这个问题。

sentences.en: For years, lots of stories, in English, at least, assumed that boys went out and did adventurous things and girls stayed at home and played with dolls.
sentences.zh: 多年来，许多英文故事——至少在英语国家——默认男孩外出冒险，而女孩则待在家里玩洋娃娃。

sentences.en: I was amazed how many books were targeted at just one sex or the other.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，竟有如此多的书籍明确只面向某一性别。

sentences.en: Of course this reflects society as it is it when the books are written.
sentences.zh: 当然，这反映了书籍创作时的社会现实。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: That's true.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 没错。

sentences.en: So it sounds as though you think it's a good course.
sentences.zh: 所以听上去你认为这是一门不错的课程。

sentences.en: TREVOR: Definitely.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: TREVOR: Have you been reading lots of children's stories, to help you decide whether to take the course?
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 为了决定是否选修这门课，你读了很多儿童故事吗？

sentences.en: rsP
sentences.zh: rsP

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Yeah.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 是的。

sentences.en: I've gone as far back as the late seventeenth century, though know there were earlier children's stories.
sentences.zh: 我追溯到了17世纪晚期，尽管我知道更早时期已有儿童故事。

sentences.en: TREVOR: So does that mean you've read Perrault's fairy tales?
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 那么这意味着你读过佩罗的童话故事了？

sentences.en: Cinderella, The Sleeping Beauty, and so on. fEE
sentences.zh: 《灰姑娘》《睡美人》等等。fEE

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Yes.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 是的。

sentences.en: They must be important, because no stories of that type had been written.
sentences.zh: 它们一定很重要，因为此前从未出现过这类故事。

sentences.en: before, these were the first.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，这些是最早问世的此类故事。

sentences.en: Then there's The Swiss Family Robinson.
sentences.zh: 接着还有《瑞士鲁滨逊一家》。

sentences.en: TREVOR: I haven't read that.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 我没读过这本书。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: The English name makes it sound as though Robinson is the family's surname, but a more accurate translation would be The Swiss Robinsons, because it's about a Swiss family who are shipwrecked, like Robinson Crusoe in the novel of a century earlier.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 英文书名让人误以为‘鲁滨逊’是这家人的姓氏，但更准确的译法应为《瑞士鲁滨逊一家》，因为它讲述的是一户瑞士家庭遭遇海难的故事，与一个世纪前小说中的鲁滨逊·克鲁索类似。

sentences.en: TREVOR: Well never knew that!
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 我以前可完全不知道这一点！

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Have you read Hoffmann's The Nutcracker and the Mouse King?
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 你读过霍夫曼的《胡桃夹子与老鼠王》吗？

sentences.en: TREVOR: Wasn't that the basis for Tchaikovsky's ballet The Nutcracker?
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 这不就是柴可夫斯基芭蕾舞剧《胡桃夹子》的创作基础吗？

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: That's right.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 没错。

sentences.en: It has some quite bizarre elements.
sentences.zh: 其中包含一些相当离奇的元素。

sentences.en: TREVOR: hope you've read Oscar Wilde's The Happy Prince.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 希望你读过奥斯卡·王尔德的《快乐王子》。

sentences.en: It's probably my favourite children's story of all time.
sentences.zh: 它大概是我有史以来最钟爱的儿童故事。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Mine too!
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 我也是！

sentences.en: And it's so surprising, because iS Wilde is best known for his plays, and most of them are very witty, but The Happy Prince iS really moving.
sentences.zh: 而且这真令人惊讶，因为王尔德最为人熟知的是他的戏剧作品，而这些戏剧大多极为机智诙谐，但《快乐王子》却格外感人至深。

sentences.en: L struggled with Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings - three long books, and I gave up after one.
sentences.zh: 我读托尔金的《魔戒》三部曲时很吃力——三本篇幅很长的书，我只读完第一本就放弃了。

sentences.en: TREVOR: It's extremely popular, though.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 不过它确实极受欢迎。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Yeah, but whereas something like The Happy Prince just carried me along with it, The Lord of the Rings took more effort than I was prepared to give it.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 是啊，但像《快乐王子》这样的作品能自然而然地吸引我沉浸其中，而《魔戒》则需要投入更多精力，超出了我愿意付出的程度。

sentences.en: TREVOR: didn't find that - I love it.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 我倒没觉得如此——我特别喜欢它。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Another one I've read is War Horse.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 我还读过另一本书，叫《战马》。

sentences.en: TREVOR: Oh yes.
sentences.zh: TREVOR: 哦，对。

sentences.en: It's about the First World War, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 它是关于第一次世界大战的，对吧？

sentences.en: Hardly what you'd expect for a children's story.
sentences.zh: 这几乎完全不符合人们对儿童故事的预期。

sentences.en: STEPHANIE: Exactly, but it's been very successful.
sentences.zh: STEPHANIE: 没错，但它却取得了巨大成功。

sentences.en: Have you read any ...
sentences.zh: 你读过任何……
